research_scope: Five complete source-free reviews of groupoids, indexed morphism families, preadditive categories and strict representable/category-valued presheaves.

amendments.review_rationale: Reviewed groupoid as a small category for which every morphism has a two-sided inverse, retaining both composition equations and excluding unrelated graph-theoretic groupoid senses.
amendments.reason: Read entire independent category-theory formulation, distinguished external defining functor data from reusable categorical prerequisites, and preserved earlier category-size corrections.

references.context: Category theory: inverse arrow g:Y→X of isomorphism f:X→Y satisfies gf=id_X and fg=id_Y, not ring multiplication.
references.reason: Inverse arrows are reusable in general categorical isomorphisms and groupoids; compare with existing categorical-isomorphism missing candidate.
references.matching_note: Provisional source-free classification; contextual candidate equivalence review required.

references.context: Category theory: f:X→Y is an isomorphism iff there exists g:Y→X with gf=id_X and fg=id_Y; no underlying-set bijectivity is assumed.
references.reason: Categorical isomorphisms are reusable structures; the groupoid axiom requires all arrows to be such isomorphisms.
references.matching_note: Provisional source-free classification; contextual candidate equivalence review required.

references.disposition: The universal condition distinguishing groupoids from general small categories, not a source of an independent 'group action' interpretation.

amendments.review_rationale: Read indexed family of arrows to common category object U, retaining potentially empty index set, distinct source objects and duplicate arrow occurrences.
amendments.reason: Read entire independent category-theory formulation, distinguished external defining functor data from reusable categorical prerequisites, and preserved earlier category-size corrections.

references.disposition: An arbitrary, possibly empty indexing set is part of the indexed family's given structural data, not a separately defined mathematical construction.
Choosing for each index a domain object and arrow to common target U is precisely the indexed-family construction; objects and morphisms come from the linked category.
Equal underlying arrows with different index labels count as separate occurrences.

amendments.review_rationale: Reviewed preadditive category as category with abelian-group hom-sets and bilinear composition, not assuming smallness or finite products from the stronger additive-category notion.
amendments.reason: Read entire independent category-theory formulation, distinguished external defining functor data from reusable categorical prerequisites, and preserved earlier category-size corrections.

references.context: Category theory: ordinary category with objects, morphisms, identities and associative composition, without requiring its collection of objects to be a set; any size assumptions are stated separately.
references.matching_note: Source occurrence 'ambient category C' denotes an ordinary category without a smallness requirement. Existing small-category meaning is too restrictive; do not conflate a fibred category, groupoid or slice category with the ambient category.

references.context: Category theory: hom-collection Hom_C(X,Y) of arrows X→Y; a preadditive category requires these collections to be sets carrying abelian group structures, without requiring all objects to form a set.
references.reason: Hom-sets are reusable categorical data; locally small and small categories are different size conventions.
references.matching_note: Provisional source-free classification; contextual candidate equivalence review required.

references.phrase: composition Hom(Y,Z) x Hom(X,Y) to Hom(X,Z)
references.disposition: The typed composition operation is already part of the ambient category; its bilinearity is the defining preadditive axiom and is already linked to bilinear maps.
Finite products and an underlying object set are not additional hypotheses in this formulation.
references.phrase: not necessarily small or additive category

references.context: Category theory: set of morphisms X→U from variable X to fixed target U in a locally small category C, with the contravariant role of X retained.
references.reason: This Hom-set is a reusable categorical concept, not the represented presheaf itself.

references.context: Category theory: for g:Y→X, precomposition sends Hom_C(X,U)→Hom_C(Y,U), f↦f∘g, respecting identity arrows and composition.
references.reason: Precomposition is a reusable operation acting on hom-sets; compare with general categorical composition during global audit.

references.disposition: The fixed object U is in the target slot of Hom_C(X,U); covariant Hom_C(U,−) is a different represented functor.
